title: Josh Clark's Speech from Commencement: Speeches for the Class of 2020
summary: This is a promotional feed episode from the commencement speech series "Commencement Speeches for the Class of 2020," featuring Josh Clark's virtual commencement address to graduates during the COVID-19 pandemic. The episode opens with several sponsor reads (Cal Hope emotional support line, Metro by T-Mobile, DirecTV Stream) before the speech. Josh tells graduates that they were not told the whole truth growing up, that people often show only part of the picture, and that they should decide whether something is important enough to research, and avoid passing along incomplete pictures if not. He uses a metaphor of flowers and weeds to argue that people resist admitting error, that weeds can be recognized by harm they cause, and that the people who benefit from calling a weed a flower are usually those in power. He closes by saying each human being is special and unique, that people are generally good, and that some people don't recognize weeds.

segments.title: Sponsor reads
segments.summary: Sponsor reads for Cal Hope emotional support, Metro by T-Mobile 5G plans, and DirecTV Stream.

segments.title: Commencement opening
segments.summary: The host welcomes graduates to the virtual commencement, notes the traditional graduation day was put on hold, and introduces Josh Clark as speaker.

segments.title: Hidden truths and incomplete pictures
segments.summary: Josh tells graduates they were not told the whole truth by parents and teachers, that people show only part of the picture to sway them, and that they must learn to think for themselves and do their own research.

segments.title: Deciding what is worth searching for
segments.summary: Josh advises deciding whether something is important enough to research; if not, shrug it off and avoid passing along an incomplete picture to others.

segments.title: Flowers and weeds metaphor
segments.summary: Josh uses a metaphor of flowers and weeds to explain how people resist admitting error, how harm reveals a weed, and how those who benefit from the false label defend it while others who called it a weed go unheard.

segments.title: Human uniqueness and goodness
segments.summary: Josh concludes that people are special and unique because they are human, that all life is valuable, and that human beings are generally good even if some do harm.

segments.title: Closing and podcast promotion
segments.summary: Closing remarks and a promotion for the Commencement Podcast on iHeart Radio.
